mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and electrolyte wasting (particularly potassium and magnesium), while eplerenone is a potassium-sparing aldosterone antagonist that increases potassium retention, creating opposing effects on potassium homeostasis and renal function.
action: Monitor serum potassium, magnesium, and renal function closely; consider alternative antifungal if possible; adjust eplerenone dose or discontinue if hyperkalemia or renal impairment develops.
